intro: Welcome to Kula, a historic town in Manisa province, from the 18th–19th century. Set among volcanic cones, it keeps more than six hundred listed Ottoman houses, and its street pattern has barely changed.
history: More than six hundred listed Ottoman houses survive in this town on the volcanic ground of Manisa. Its street pattern has barely changed: bow-fronted houses, stone courtyard walls and narrow lanes have been kept together. All around, the extinct cones and lava flows form a UNESCO Global Geopark.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the bow-fronted Kula houses, the Kula mosque, the stone courtyard walls and the volcanic ground itself.
facts: Did you know? Human footprints found in the lava nearby are about ten thousand years old — the oldest human traces known in Anatolia. And in the town itself, more than six hundred listed Ottoman houses survive, along a street pattern that has barely changed.
outro: This brings our tour of Kula to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water. Take your time in these lanes on your way out. Enjoy your visit.
